title: sre: adaptive load-shedding + regional failover hardening and circuit-breaker fix
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We observed a sequence of cross-region latency spikes that caused one region to exhaust available worker slots and then trigger aggressive failover to a neighboring region. That region then experienced transient saturation and entered a degraded state, producing a cascading degradation loop. This change introduces an adaptive per-region load-shedding policy tied to short-window SLO signals, hardens the circuit-breaker state transitions to avoid stuck OPEN states after partial capacity loss, and adds a conservative regional fallback backoff to prevent oscillation. The change is gated behind a feature flag (ops.feature_flags.regional_adaptive_shed) and is rolled out as a canary followed by a full rollout. Checklist: 1) Implement adaptive load-shedding controller that computes shed probability from recent error rate and P99 latency SLO windows; 2) Add token-based pre-queue throttle to protect control plane and auth services; 3) Fix circuit-breaker state machine bug where HALF_OPEN transitions could be skipped when a subset of shards returned inconsistent health; 4) Add metrics (region_load_shed_percent, region_cb_state, region_fallback_backoff_seconds) and tracing hooks for incident investigation; 5) Add integration test that simulates partial region outage and asserts no failover oscillation; 6) Docs and ops runbook updates; 7) Hotfix: fix a race that could keep fallback backoff at zero on rapid repeated failovers. Why this matters: reduces user-facing error spikes during regional disturbances, preserves global availability by limiting blast radius and preventing cascading failovers. Rollout plan: enable feature flag in canary region (eu-west-1) for 48h, monitor region_load_shed_percent and request latency/error SLOs, then enable globally if no regressions. If regressions occur, toggle feature flag off and rollback via the existing deployment pipeline. Related: SUP-412 was opened during the incident window and contains patient repro steps for the CI smoke failures we observed.
commit_summary: 7 commits: initial adaptive shed controller + config; add token pre-queue throttle; fix circuit-breaker state machine race; add metrics and traces; integration test for regional failover; docs and ops-runbook; bump feature flag default to off
review_thread: Ethan Park: Requesting clarification: can you explain how the shed probability maps to token-level rejects? Is it deterministic per-request?

Priya Nair: The shed probability is sampled per-request at the admission point. We use a deterministic hash+probability when request has a stable id to avoid flapping for retries; otherwise we sample per-call. Added notes in load_shedding.rs comments.
Sasha McDermott: Can the circuit-breaker fix be toggled independently? If it stays merged we want the ability to revert only the adaptive shedding if we see new patterns.

Priya Nair: Yes, circuit-breaker state machine change is controlled by ops.flags.cb_state_harden and defaults to true because it fixes a correctness bug; adaptive shedding is behind regional_adaptive_shed and defaults to false. Documented in deploy/feature_flags.yaml.
Liam O'Connell: Integration test looks good but flaked on first run in CI due to timing; please make timeouts slightly looser and add a deterministic seed.
Priya Nair: Adjusted test timeouts and added seeded RNG to the test harness to make result reproducible. Reran locally and in CI.
Ethan Park: LGTM after CI pass
release_notes: Added adaptive regional load-shedding with an ops feature flag, hardened the circuit-breaker state machine to avoid stuck OPEN states during partial regional loss, and added telemetry for region_load_shed_percent and circuit-breaker state. Default behavior unchanged until feature flag enabled.
notes_for_oncall: If enabled and you observe sudden increase in region_load_shed_percent without corresponding CPU/GPU saturation, toggle ops.feature_flags.regional_adaptive_shed off to restore prior behavior and open SUP-412 for follow-up. Use region_cb_state metric to determine per-region circuit breaker health.
changelog_entry: sre: adaptive load-shedding and circuit-breaker hardening (feature-flagged) - reduces cascading failovers during regional disturbances
testing_notes: Canary tested in eu-west-1 for 48h with synthetic traffic that injected a 30% worker availability loss; no oscillations observed. Integration test simulates shard inconsistency and asserts circuit-breaker recovers to CLOSED only after controlled HALF_OPEN probe. See tests/integration/regional_failover_test.go for scenarios.
deploy_instructions: 1) Merge to main, 2) Toggle ops.feature_flags.regional_adaptive_shed=true for canary region via ops console, 3) Monitor metrics for 48h, 4) If stable, enable globally in stages by region. Rollback: toggle flag false and redeploy if necessary.
extras: observability: added dashboard panel 'Regional Load Shedding'
